content: Carboxymethyl cellulose is an ophthalmologic agent approved by the FDA for the treatment of burning, irritation, and discomfort caused by dryness of the eye. It is also indicated for temporary relief of symptoms due to exposure to wind or sun and may serve as a protectant against further irritation. Common adverse reactions include eye pain, changes in vision, and eye irritation. If these symptoms persist or worsen, or if redness and irritation continue for more than 72 hours, it is advised to stop use and consult a healthcare provider. For administration, the product is intended for external use only. To avoid contamination, the tip of the container should not touch any surface, including the eye. The solution should not be reused, and any opened container must be discarded. If the solution changes color or becomes cloudy, it should not be used. The recommended dosage involves instilling 1 or 2 drops into the affected eye(s) as needed. For specific conditions such as post-LASIK dryness, follow the instructions provided by your eye doctor. There is limited information regarding off-label uses, contraindications, and drug interactions for carboxymethyl cellulose. Similarly, there is no FDA guidance on its use in specific populations, including pregnant or nursing women, pediatric or geriatric patients, individuals with renal or hepatic impairment, or immunocompromised patients. The pharmacological mechanism of action for carboxymethyl cellulose is not well-documented. It functions as an eye lubricant and contains inactive ingredients such as calcium chloride, magnesium chloride, potassium chloride, purified water, sodium chloride, and sodium lactate. Hydrochloric acid or sodium hydroxide may be included to adjust pH. There is no established interaction between carboxymethyl cellulose and alcohol. Patients are advised to consult their healthcare provider regarding the effects of alcohol consumption while using this medication. The product is marketed under the brand name CARBOXYMETHYLCELLULOSE SODIUM®. There is limited information available regarding look-alike drug names or storage instructions for this medication.
